newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 31.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- The Dow Jones industrials are poised to end higher for the sixth year in a row.
- Stock and mutual fund investors have been cutting back on their purchases this month after putting a robust $17.1 billion into stock funds in November.
- Tandy will dispose of its 17-store Incredible Universe electronics chain and close 19 of it 113 Computer City stores.
- Banc One agreed to acquire Oklahoma's Liberty Bancorp in a stock swap valued at about $544 million.
- Takeover premiums have fallen by more than half since 1990.
- Next Software has not had a profit on operations for at least three years, according to internal documents for the company Apple has just agreed to acquire in a nearly $400 million deal.
- The index of leading economic indicators rose 0.1 percent in November.
- Sales of existing homes rose 1.8 percent in November from October.
- The deregulation of hospital prices in New York state will trigger $2 billion a year in additional taxes for employers and insurance companies.
- Humana said it plans to eliminate up to 900 jobs.
- Texaco could unexpectedly be subject to government scrutiny following settlement of its race bias suit.
- Circus Circus is to unveil plans for its biggest casino project ever, a 4,000-room Las Vegas resort.
- Steelcase was ordered to pay rival office furniture maker Haworth $211.5 million in one of the biggest patent infringement awards in U.S. history.
- Shares of Aegon rose 10 percent in Big Board trading after it confirmed plans to purchase Providian 's insurance lines.
- Zitel shares fell 33 percent after officials close to investor George Soros said he had not bought the stock, despite rumors he was amassing a stake.
- Stronger-than-expected economic news pushed the bond market off modest, quickly-scaled peaks Monday.
- With the stock market soaring this year, the record level of takeover activity is less of a boon to investors than in years gone by because buyers are getting more tightfisted.
